subject: Acme Health: bake-off criteria, pain summary & next tests
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Lydia Park <lydia.park@acmehealth.com>, Ken Morales <ken.morales@acmehealth.com>
Cc: 
Date: Mon, 03 May 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Acme Health: bake-off criteria, pain summary & next tests

Thanks for the time today — appreciate Lydia walking us through the current workflow. Below is a concise recap from my side and proposed next tests so we’re aligned heading into the vendor bake-off.

Quick summary of the pain points you shared:
- Slow inference for batch analytics (20–30s/query) impacting clinician dashboards
- Cost unpredictability during monthly spikes (weekend surges from data reindexing)
- Need for deterministic latency under 300ms for triage endpoints
- Enterprise constraints: SSO + audit logs, data residency option for PHI

Goals we heard:
- Get median latency under 250ms for 95% of triage calls in production
- Reduce per-token inference cost by 30% vs current provider during steady-state
- Deliver a test plan that validates SSO + SOC2 evidence for procurement

Decision criteria (what you said you’d weigh):
1) Latency SLA (tail/median)
2) Cost economics at 5M tokens/month baseline & burst behavior
3) Security/compliance fit (SAML, audit logs, private deployment option)
4) Integration/engineering effort (SDKs, rollout controls)
5) Support/enterprise SLAs

Proposed bake-off tests (what Redwood will run / coordinate):
- Latency sweep: run 1K synthetic triage requests with real prompt lengths (50–350 tokens). Measure median, p95, p99. (Owner: Marissa/Rishi)
- Burst scenario: simulate weekend batch surge (x5 request rate) and verify graceful degradation + fallback to smaller model. (Owner: Aditya)
- Cost simulation: run tokenized replay of typical month and compare unit cost across Redwood vs VertexCloud and NovaInference. (Owner: Marissa)
- Integration check: SAML SSO test + audit log export (non-prod) and sample retention policy. (Owner: Sean)

Open questions we need from your side:
1) Can you share a redacted sample of the triage prompts (PII removed) so we can seed realistic tests?
2) Any constraints on allowed cloud regions for the private deployment?
3) Procurement timeline & contract approver (name/email) — Ken, is there an expected cutover window?

Attachments: acme-eval-matrix.xlsx (attachment)

Next steps I’m proposing:
- I’ll schedule the latency sweep for Wed (5/5) — Marissa/Rishi will own execution and share results by EOD Thu (5/6).
- Aditya will draft a short script to simulate weekend surge; will run in parallel.
- Sean will share a checklist for SSO/audit evidence and a time estimate for the integration run.

If this matches your read, can you confirm the sample prompts and procurement approver by EOD Tue?

Thanks again,

--
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | (555) 555-0123

From: Lydia Park <lydia.park@acmehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Ken Morales <ken.morales@acmehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 04 May 2027 09:21:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Acme Health: bake-off criteria, pain summary & next tests

Thanks Marissa — that’s a great summary. Couple quick clarifications from our side: 

- We can provide a redacted set of ~300 triage prompts by EOD Wednesday (5/5). Will remove PHI.
- For regions, our preference is US-EAST for production; testing can be in US-EAST or US-WEST.
- Procurement: Ken Morales is the approver; primary procurement contact is "ProcureOps" (procureops@acmehealth.com). We’re aiming for a vendor selection by 2027-06-15 and a pilot kickoff in late June.

Two asks from our security team before we run tests:
1) Can Redwood provide a sample SOC2-observability export (fields and format) we can validate?
2) For the burst test — please confirm what fallback behavior looks like (model degrade strategy vs queueing).

Samir from VertexCloud copied us; he wanted to confirm his team will share their baseline numbers as well.

We look forward to the latency sweep — let us know time window so we can confirm access.

Regards,
Lydia Park
Director, Clinical Products | Acme Health
lydia.park@acmehealth.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: aditya_rao <aditya@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, sean_gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Wed, 05 May 2027 08:03:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Acme Health: bake-off criteria, pain summary & next tests

Internal note — forwarding Lydia's confirmation and next asks. High priority POC; procurement timeline is aggressive (selection ~6/15). Key asks below and my recommended assignments: 

1) Latency sweep (Wed 5/5 window): Rishi, can you run the 1K triage set with 95% real prompt distribution? Focus on median/p95/p99 and GPU config used. Deliverable: csv with per-request latencies + summary. (Owner: rishi_malhotra)

2) Burst test (x5 rate) with fallback strategy documentation: Aditya, run both continuous-batching and a degrade-to-smaller-model scenario. Capture tail latency and throughput. (Owner: aditya_rao)

3) SSO/audit checklist: Sean, send the exact sample export (schema) and steps to reproduce SAML test. Lydia asked for "SOC2-observability export" sample. (Owner: sean_gallagher)

4) Competitive baseline: I’ll coordinate to get VertexCloud & NovaInference baseline numbers (Samir is on the thread). We should ensure we highlight where Redwood wins: private deployment option, graceful fallback, and cost controls.

Attachments: bakeoff-test-plan.md (internal test steps)

Open operational questions we should answer in the first delivery:
- Disk-backed KV cache expectations (how we handle cache warm/colder cold-starts)
- Tokenization parity notes for cost sim (we should state tokenizer versions used)

Timeline: run tests today (Wed 5/5) and share preliminary results by EOD Thu (5/6). I’ll book a 30-min sync Fri 5/7 10:00–10:30 PT to review. Please confirm owners and any blockers.

Thanks — Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

I’ll take the latency sweep. Plan:
- Use the 300 prompts Lydia will provide plus 700 synthetic draws matching token distribution (50–350 tokens).
- Run on c5-gpu-4 (prod-like) and measure per-request latency with and without KV cache warm.
- Produce p50/p95/p99 and per-config CSV by EOD Thu.

Two quick asks to run this cleanly:
1) Please confirm which tokenizer/version to use for token-count parity.
2) Provide sample workload header (auth token or test API key) to avoid throttling.

I’ll post results to the Drive link once done.

—Rishi
